title: Algebraic modular forms, Part II: Siegel forms modulo pⁿ
summary: Extend the parent’s modular-curve direction to integral genus-two Siegel forms, arbitrary torsion coefficients and K/O. Nine layers give the all-component Fourier interface, primary and secondary Hasse geometry, coefficient operators and corrected Q₂, integral geometric Hecke actions, characteristic-p theta and ordinary full-frame comparison. Existing bundle, BT₁, compactification and primary-Hasse owners are imported. This is a completed planning pass with precise open supplier requests and six mathematical verification gaps; it is not a closed or implemented roadmap. The independent generic GL₃ direction is proposed as a separate roadmap.
readme: Nine target layers extend the parent after R15.6. Use (j,k) for highest weights and Ω(d,r)=ω(d+r,r), keep all components, and normalize at-p correspondences before coefficient reduction. The full reader gives each target, hypothesis, proof route, API, discriminating tests and source locator. Coverage is planned with explicit supplier and mathematical verification obligations. The independent GL₃ brief is preserved as a split proposal.

stages.title: Integral forms and Fourier expansions
stages.description:
Build the genus-two section and expansion interface over arbitrary O-modules, importing the existing genus-two bundles and compactifications. The section lattice, all-component expansion principle and covariance are the common input to both geometric and formal operators.

Targets:
- Integral Siegel forms and cusp forms: Fix neat tame level K^p and hyperspecial level at p. On the imported smooth toroidal Siegel threefold X over O, let E=e*Ω¹_G/X and λ=det E. For integers j≥k put ω(j,k)=Sym^(j−k)E⊗λ^k and ω(j,k)^sub=ω(j,k)⊗I_D, using the imported bundles. For every O-module M define M_(j,k)(M)=H⁰(X,ω(j,k)⊗_O M) and S_(j,k)(M)=H⁰(X,ω(j,k)^sub⊗_O M). All components are retained. Ω(d,r)=ω(d+r,r). The notation H⁰ with M=K/O means the sheaf tensor product, not a tensor of H⁰ with K/O.
- Fourier indices and change of variables: At a marked split zero-dimensional cusp with tame denominator bound L^e, use Q=(m,r,n), representing mx²+rxy+ny² and the half-integral matrix [[m,r/2],[r/2,n]]. Here m,r,n∈L^(−e)Z, m,n≥0 and Δ(Q)=r²−4mn≤0. The denominators are prime to p. For M∈GL₂(Q) set M·Q=(det M)^(−1)MQMᵗ; in particular Δ(M·Q)=Δ(Q). Coefficients outside the allowed semidefinite, tame-denominator index lattice are zero. A form is p-primitive precisely when its three p-integral coefficients are not all divisible by p.
- Fourier expansions on every component: For a tame cyclotomic faithfully flat extension O′/O, choose a split cusp on every geometric connected component and a Mumford torus frame. Restriction defines coefficients a_c(F,Q)∈Sym^(j−k)(O′²)⊗M, with the determinant factor trivialized by that frame. Their support lies in the preceding index set with one fixed tame denominator bound. For L=1 the ambient series module embeds in (O′⊗M)[ζ,ζ⁻¹][[q,q′]] with finite Laurent support in ζ for each (q,q′) slice. Use the completed cone-monoid modules on charts, glued over faces; do not use a Laurent localization of a three-variable power-series ring. At a cusp stabilizer Γ̄⊂SL₂(Z) of level prime to p, a_c(F,M·Q)=Sym^(j−k)(M)a_c(F,Q). On another marked frame or component, include the induced coefficient transport.
- Integral q-expansion principle: The family of expansion maps on one cusp of each geometric connected component is injective for every O-module M. For M=O, a rational section of ω(j,k) or its subcanonical extension whose coefficients at all these cusps are integral belongs to the integral global-section lattice. More generally, divisibility of an integral section by ϖ^m is equivalent to divisibility of all its coefficients. This is a statement about sections and their saturated lattice, not a surjectivity assertion for arbitrary formal series.

stages.title: Rank strata and the primary Hasse invariant
stages.description:
Separate the closed primary-Hasse zero scheme from its rank-one open. Record the precise rank geometry used later, with an explicit gap for the comparison of reduction-theory coordinates and the existing moduli models. Import the primary invariant rather than defining it again.

Targets:
- Rank strata and scheme structures: For X₁=X⊗k₀ and X_par,1 define the rank-r stratum by multiplicative rank r∈{0,1,2} of the semiabelian fiber; rank at most r and rank at least r have their inclusive meanings. On abelian fibers this equals the p-rank. Write S=V(h) for the scheme cut out by the imported primary Hasse section h∈H⁰(X₁,λ^(p−1)); later define Z₂=V_S(h′). Write Z_red for the reduced rank-zero locus and SS for the finite superspecial subset of the abelian interior. The same conventions with subscript par apply to X_par,1. For X_n use the rank loci in its underlying special-fiber space; S itself is a characteristic-p closed subscheme.
- Dimensions and supersingular geometry: At both spherical and paramodular level, the rank-r stratum is dense in its rank-at-most-r closure and has pure dimension r+1. At spherical level X₁ is smooth, S is a pure surface and Z_red is a curve disjoint from the toroidal boundary. SS is finite; V* has rank one on S minus SS. Over an algebraic closure, every irreducible component C of Z_red is P¹, contains p²+1 distinct superspecial points, and has E|_C≅O(−1)⊕O(p), hence λ|_C≅O(p−1). The assertions about this splitting and component counts are for spherical good level; no analogous paramodular splitting is asserted.
- Simple Hasse zeros at rank one: The nonordinary zero schemes S and S_par are reduced effective Cartier divisors. In the rank-one crystalline basis e₁,e₂,e₃,e₄ with F e₁=p e₁, F e₂=−p e₃, F e₃=e₂ and F e₄=e₄, choose the alternating pairing with ⟨e₁,e₄⟩=⟨e₂,e₃⟩=1. A first-order Hodge lift generated by columns (1,0,X,W) and (0,1,Y,Z) has Hasse linear term −Y. The principal tangent equation X=Z, and the two paramodular equations Z=0 and X=0, leave Y free. Thus h vanishes simply at every generic point of the nonordinary divisor. Normality of the ambient special fiber and Cohen–Macaulayness give reducedness globally.
- Hasse expansion and multiplication: At every split cusp the imported primary Hasse section has Fourier expansion 1. It is a nonzerodivisor on X₁ because the ordinary locus is dense on every component. Multiplication by h therefore injects M_(j,k)(k₀) and S_(j,k)(k₀) into weight (j+p−1,k+p−1), for any j≥k. It commutes with prime-to-p Hecke correspondences under the natural coefficient maps and with tame deck transformations. The determinant Hasse ideal used on an integral Hilbert modular chart is locally (p,h) after specializing the same semiabelian determinant, with its chosen Hodge trivialization; it is not a different invariant.

stages.title: The secondary Hasse invariant
stages.description:
Construct h′ intrinsically from the rank-one BT₁ filtration, prove duality and the normal extension calculation, then glue over the nonordinary divisor and boundary. Distinguish its order-two zero scheme from the reduced supersingular curve; the odd-p global square root is a separate, conditional target.

Targets:
- Secondary Hasse invariant on rank one: Over a reduced F_p-scheme B let G be a height-four, dimension-two BT₁ with constant multiplicative and étale ranks both one. Import G^m⊂G^o⊂G and put G^oo=G^o/G^m. The imported crystal of G^oo gives an isomorphism v:(ω_((G^oo)^D))^∨→(ω_(G^oo))^p induced by V*. Taking v^(p−1) and the Fargues determinant identification LF defines h′(G^oo) in ω_G^oo^(p²−1). Define h′(G)=Ha(G^m)^(p+1)⊗h′(G^oo) in (det ω_G)^(p²−1). It is a unit on B. The same recipe applies to the connected height-three, dimension-two BT₁ with multiplicative rank one and biconnected quotient of height two, to handle the boundary; its duality claim is only made in the height-four case.
- Secondary Hasse duality: For the height-four input above, LF^(p+1):(det ω_G)^(p²−1)≅(det ω_G^D)^(p²−1) sends h′(G) to h′(G^D). An étale isogeny of Barsotti–Tate groups identifies both primary and secondary sections wherever the latter is defined. These equalities survive their unique extensions to reduced normal bases.
- Canonical subgroup in the Frobenius kernel: Let B be reduced normal, G a height-four dimension-two BT₁, generically of multiplicative and étale ranks one, and suppose ker(V*:ω_G→ω_G^(p)) is an invertible direct summand. Set K=ker(V:G[F]^(p)→G[F]). Then K is finite flat of rank p and H=G[F]^(p)/K embeds as a finite flat rank-p subgroup of G[F], extending G^m from the rank-one open. Apply the same construction to G^D to obtain L. Let N=ω_(G[F]/H) and N_D=ω_(G^D[F]/L). The Hodge diagram defines V_H*:ω_H→ω_H^p, W:N^p→coker(V*), and Z:N_D^∨→coker(V*); all three are maps between line bundles. The source of Z uses coker(F*)≅N_D^∨; Z is an isomorphism, since the full crystalline V* has image ω_G^(p) and kernel im F*.
- Normal-base extension of secondary Hasse: Under the preceding normal-base hypotheses, h′ extends uniquely across B. Its support of zeros is the complement of the open where both multiplicative and étale ranks are one. To construct it, use A=(V_H*)^(p+1)⊗(W⁻¹Z)^(p−1) and the analogous B_D for the dual. A is regular, with zeros exactly where multiplicative rank is zero; B_D has zeros where étale rank is zero. Their product, under LF and determinant identifications, extends (h′)². Normality then extends the rational section h′ itself. If the two ranks agree at every point, both individual zero-locus descriptions reduce to the same rank-zero set.
- Local models of the nonordinary surface: Off SS, the spherical nonordinary surface is smooth and is identified via H⊂G[F] with the indicated rank-one Iwahori strata. In the supplied local-model ring R=F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy,ax+by+abc), its chart is R/(a,y,x+bc)≅F_p[b,c]. For the paramodular surface off SS, the two branches are obtained from R/(x,y+ac)≅F_p[a,b,c] by a=0 and b=0. Their reduced union is Spec F_p[a,b,c]/(ab), with rank-one open D(a)∪D(b). The two branches meet along a=b=0. The initial quotient R/(x,y+ac) alone is the ambient three-space, not the nonordinary surface.
- Secondary Hasse on both nonordinary divisors: The rank-one secondary sections for G and G′ extend uniquely to h′∈H⁰(S,λ^(p²−1)) and h′_par∈H⁰(S_par,λ_par^(p²−1)). At torus-rank-one boundary points use the connected height-three BT₁ recipe. Off SS, extend on the spherical normal chart; on the paramodular nodal chart extend on each normal branch and glue because both restrictions vanish on their intersection. Across the finite set SS use Cohen–Macaulay Hartogs on the surface. The support of V(h′) is Z_red and likewise at paramodular level. This is the single secondary section used here; CG20’s auxiliary section is compared only after specifying its normalization or power.
- Reduced supersingular divisor and square root: For odd p on the spherical nonordinary surface S, there is a secondary root b∈H⁰(S,λ^((p²−1)/2)), with normalization fixed so that b²=h′; it cuts out Z_red as an effective Cartier divisor. Thus V(h′)=2 Z_red as effective Cartier divisors. State the existence and normalization first over an algebraically closed residue field and descend only with its verified descent datum. At p=2 the half-integer Hodge exponent is unavailable; h′ itself remains defined, and no integral-half-weight root statement is included. No square-root theorem at paramodular level is inferred from the spherical one.
- Normalized pullback of Hasse sections: Let λ_G:G→G′ be an isogeny of Barsotti–Tate groups in characteristic p with constant multiplicative rank, ker λ_G=L⊂G[p], and suppose at every geometric point G[p]=H_x⊕L_x with H_x multiplicative. There is a canonical determinant-line isomorphism λ̃*:det ω_G′→det ω_G. On the multiplicative parts use the imported normalized determinant of the character-lattice isogeny. On the quotient by the multiplicative part write the induced isogeny uniquely as pµ with µ an isomorphism and use µ*. Tensor these two maps. The result preserves h and h′ wherever defined and hence their unique normal extensions.

stages.title: Hasse lifts and torsion weight shifts
stages.description:
Lift a positive power of the primary invariant, prove its coefficient-adic power congruences and torsion weight-shift injection. The two-affine cover uses descended sections on the minimal compactification, whose secondary-section comparison remains an explicit gap.

Targets:
- Characteristic-zero Hasse power lifts: There exist r>0 and A∈H⁰(X,λ^(r(p−1))) reducing to h^r. They are obtained by lifting a sufficiently high Hasse power on the minimal compactification, where an appropriate power of λ is ample, and pulling back. A is a chosen lift, with no canonicality asserted. It pulls back to every tame auxiliary-level model. For prescribed j≥k and m≥1 one may choose arbitrarily large s divisible by p^(m−1); multiplication by A^s then raises both weights by t=rs(p−1) modulo ϖ^m.
- Canonical powers modulo pⁿ: If two local lifts a,b of the same mod-p section of a line bundle differ by p, then a^(p^(n−1))≡b^(p^(n−1)) mod p^n. Consequently h^(p^(n−1)) has a canonical lift to X⊗Z/p^n in λ^(p^(n−1)(p−1)), obtained by taking local lifts and gluing their powers. Over a ramified O the analogous statement for a−b∈ϖO is a^(p^(m−1))≡b^(p^(m−1)) mod ϖ^m. Thus A^s modulo ϖ^m depends only on h^r whenever p^(m−1) divides s. It commutes with pullback, including prime-to-p isogenies identifying the determinant sections.
- Equivariant torsion weight shifts: For j≥k, m≥1 and the chosen r,A, let s>0 be divisible by p^(m−1), and t=rs(p−1). Multiplication by A^s is injective from M_(j,k)(O/ϖ^m) to M_(j+t,k+t)(O/ϖ^m), and likewise for cusp forms. It is equivariant for prime-to-p Hecke correspondences, their tame-level U operators, and auxiliary deck transformations. Arbitrarily large t of this form are possible.
- Two affine opens above rank at least one: Let 𝔛* be the formal minimal spherical compactification. Descend h to its special fiber and h′ to the closed nonordinary divisor V(p,h). For sufficiently divisible and sufficiently large N, these supply noncanonical sections s₁,s₂ of the same ample line L=λ^(N(p²−1)) on 𝔛*: s₁ reduces to h^(N(p+1)), and s₂ restricts on V(p,h) to (h′)^N. Their nonzero formal loci cover precisely 𝔛*^{≥1}=D(s₁)∪D(s₂), and each is affine. This construction owns the spherical cover; the inverse-image Klingen cover and its cohomological resolution belong to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.

stages.title: Formal coefficient operators and Q₂
stages.description:
Keep the coefficient combinatorics on a formal module separate from geometric modularity. Fix the discriminant sign, normalized binary-form action, determinant-p cosets and two different operators denoted U₂ in the sources. Cancel the rational expression for Q₂ before any finite-coefficient reduction.

Targets:
- Covariant formal Siegel series: For a coefficient O-module C_d=Sym^d(O²)⊗M, d≥0, a formal Siegel series is a coefficient function Q↦a(Q) on the S1 index lattice, extended by zero outside it, with a(γ·Q)=ρ_d(γ)a(Q) for γ∈Γ̄. Use the actual semidefinite support and fixed tame denominator bound; all-component series carry the source/target cusp transports of the fixed level. This defines a module. A series need not be the expansion of a geometric form. The action ρ_d extends to integral 2×2 matrices via the existing symmetric-power functor; determinant weight is recorded in the operator scalars.
- Determinant-p cosets and integral neighbors: Let Γ̄ be a congruence subgroup of SL₂(Z) of level prime to p. Import the generic double-coset and index-p lattice machinery from current TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms Layer 2. The left cosets MΓ̄ in Γ̄ diag(p,1) Γ̄ have p+1 integral representatives M of determinant p and are parametrized by P¹(F_p). For the full group one may take diag(1,p) and [[p,a],[0,1]] for 0≤a<p, with the chosen action on Q; at general level choose compatible lifts by prime-to-p approximation. Only terms with M⁻¹·Q p-integral contribute. The associated projective line is the one on which the reduction of Q must vanish; specify it through this integrality criterion rather than an ambiguous kernel/image convention.
- The formal U, Z and V operators: For formal series define (UF)(Q)=a(F,pQ), (VF)(Q)=a(F,Q/p) with zero extension, and (ZF)(Q)=Σ_M ρ_d(M)a(F,M⁻¹·Q), summed over the determinant-p representatives. Define Z₂=UZ, so (Z₂F)(Q)=Σ_Mρ_d(M)a(F,M⁻¹·pQ). These operators preserve integral coefficient modules and covariance, with the all-component Hecke transport attached when the level has multiple components. They satisfy UV=1, Z₂=UZ, and UZ₂=Z₂U. No identity UZ=ZU is asserted.
- Discriminant diagonal operator X₂: Assume p odd. Over O, define X₂ on the Q-coefficient by the integer scalar ε(Q): if Q is p-primitive, ε(Q)=legendreSym(p,Δ(Q)); if Q≡0 mod p, ε(Q)=p. Define U₂=−1+pX₂. Thus its scalar is −1+p legendreSym(p,Δ(Q)) on primitive Q and −1+p² on nonprimitive Q. On characteristic-p coefficients X₂ reduces everywhere to multiplication by legendreSym(p,Δ(Q)). The sign convention is Δ=r²−4mn=−4det Q.
- Characteristic-p formal relations: Over k₀ and for odd p, UX₂=0, X₂³=X₂ and Z₂X₂=0. The first holds because pQ is nonprimitive; the second because the reduced multipliers are 0,1,−1. In Z₂X₂, every contributing index R=M⁻¹·pQ has det R=p²det Q, hence Δ(R) is divisible by p, so its X₂ coefficient vanishes. This only uses congruence of the discriminant, not det R=0 as a rational number.
- Rational Hecke decomposition and residual V₂: Fix j≥k≥2, d=j−k, and the CG20 similitude^(−3) normalization of the rational spherical double cosets T=[diag(1,1,p,p)], T₂=[diag(1,p,p,p²)] and S=[pI₄]. In the trivial central/diamond sector with its chosen component identifications, S=p^(j+k−6). Their coefficient operators satisfy T=U+p^(k−2)Z+p^(j+k−3)V and T₂=p^(j+k−6)U₂+p^(k−3)Z₂+p^(j+2k−6)V₂. Define the rational residual V₂ by the second equality, using the rational T₂ and the other defined terms. The finite-coset calculation must show it preserves the integral formal lattice and thereby extends to all coefficient modules. At a disconnected adelic level retain the central and cusp transport actions; the displayed scalar S formula requires the stated trivial sector.
- Integral corrected Q₂ operator: For j≥k≥2 in the normalization just fixed, cancel negative powers in (pT₂+(p+p³)S)p^(2−k) before reducing coefficients. The result is the integral formal operator Q₂=p^(j−2)X₂+Z₂+p^(j+k−3)V₂+p^(j−1)·1. Thus Q₂≡Z₂ mod p except at (j,k)=(2,2), where Q₂≡Z₂+X₂. The extra identity term comes from p³S and is retained in the exact integral identity. In particular at (3,3) Q₂≡Z₂ even though T₂≡Z₂−1.

stages.title: Binary quadratic neighbors
stages.description:
Retain labeled occurrences and the symmetric-power matrix weights in the neighbor multiset. The projective-zero theorem is imported; this layer specializes it to the support of Z and proves reciprocity without inverting a determinant-p matrix on coefficients.

Targets:
- Binary-form neighbor multiset: Fix the oriented double coset Δ_p=Γ̄ diag(p,1)Γ̄ from S5. For a p-integral index Q, let ℱ_Δ([Q]) (abbreviated ℱ([Q])) be the multiset of Γ̄-equivalence classes [M⁻¹·Q] contributed by the determinant-p left cosets whose transform is p-integral. Count each contributing coset once, including when different cosets give the same class. The construction depends only on [Q]. Its coefficient realization retains, for each contributing M and its transformed representative P, the intertwiner ρ_d(M): a(ZF,Q)=Σ_Mρ_d(M)a(F,P). It is not an unweighted sum of abstract orbit coefficients.
- Projective-zero count of neighbors: If Q is p-primitive and p odd, |ℱ([Q])|=1+legendreSym(p,Δ(Q)), giving 0,1,2 according as the discriminant is nonsquare, zero or a nonzero square modulo p. If Q≡0 mod p the cardinality is p+1. The bijection is between labeled admissible determinant-p cosets and zeros of Q in P¹(F_p), so the count is a multiset count.
- Reciprocity of neighbor classes: Let Δ_p^∨={pM⁻¹:M∈Δ_p}. If [P] occurs in ℱ_Δ([Q]), then [Q] occurs in ℱ_(Δ^∨)([P]). For Q=M·P the reverse action uses pM⁻¹, an integral determinant-p matrix. If Δ_p^∨=Δ_p, in particular for Γ̄=SL₂(Z), this is the symmetric relation [P]∈ℱ([Q]) iff [Q]∈ℱ([P]). At general tame level keep the reverse correspondence and cusp/diamond transport; prime-to-p level alone does not imply equality of the two double cosets. No inverse of ρ_d(M) on torsion coefficients is asserted.

stages.title: Integral geometric Hecke actions
stages.description:
Construct the minuscule operator on the rank-at-least-one formal open using ordinary trace divisibility. Use coherent Hartogs for global H⁰ and use a normalized paramodular composite for the torsion Q₂ action. Coherent duality is an explicit supplier extension, and the low-weight central subtraction is checked.

Targets:
- Finiteness of the spherical correspondence: Restrict the imported compactified C_(p,2) isogeny correspondence (Pilloni indexing; CG20 β₁) to the formal locus X^{≥1}. Both relevant projections are proper and quasi-finite, hence finite, and are generically étale. In the interior they classify isotropic Lagrangian rank-p² kernels. At a geometric ordinary or rank-one point, only finitely many such subgroups occur; positive-dimensional families of α_p-subgroups arise only on the excluded rank-zero locus. At the boundary use the imported degeneration chart. This is a restriction of the existing correspondence, not a new Hilbert-scheme construction.
- Ordinary trace divisibility: For the finite correspondence over X^{≥1}, write d=j−k≥0 and r=k≥2. On the formal neighborhood of an ordinary point the kernel types are multiplicative, mixed and étale. The differential on Ω(d,r) factors respectively through p^(d+2r), p^r and 1; the trace factors respectively through 1, p and p³. Thus the raw pullback followed by trace lands in p³Ω(d,r), including the subcanonical boundary twist. For r=2 these are the source’s p^(d+4),p²,1 differential bounds. The trace bounds are ideals/divisibility statements, not merely the degrees of maps.
- Integral normalized minuscule operator: The raw finite-correspondence sheaf map T′_(p,2):(p₁)*p₂*Ω(d,r)(−D)→Ω(d,r)(−D) has image in p³Ω(d,r)(−D) over the formal rank-at-least-one locus for d≥0,r≥2. Define T=p^(−3)T′ by the unique factorization through multiplication by p³ on the torsion-free target. This defines an integral cohomological correspondence on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1},Ω(d,r)(−D)), compatible with finite coefficients and rationalization; the same construction applies to the canonical bundle without the boundary twist. For O/ϖ^m, reduce the integral correspondence after its construction, without dividing by p on the quotient.
- Hartogs across supersingular curves: Let E₀=Ω(d,r) or Ω(d,r)(−D), with d≥0 and r any integer. For n≥1, restriction H⁰(X,E₀/ϖ^n)→H⁰(X_n^{≥1},E₀/ϖ^n) is an isomorphism and H¹ is injective. The same holds for n=∞, interpreted as coherent formal cohomology over 𝔛, and for the corresponding K/O sheaves by filtered colimits. The closed complement Z_red has codimension two in every CM thickening X_n and is disjoint from D. No H²-injectivity assertion follows.
- Integral paramodular composite correspondence: Write d=j−k≥0 and r=k≥2. On the imported spherical, Klingen and paramodular lci models, form the degree-p³ and degree-p isogeny correspondences. Their differential maps tensored with fundamental classes have integral factorizations by p^(r+2) and p respectively. Normalize these integral maps before passing to coefficients, then compose to obtain C_r on integral coherent cohomology. Rationally, in the CG20 normalization, C_r=p^(3−r)(T₂+(1+p+p²+p³)S). In the trivial central sector Q₂=C_r−(1+p²)p^(j−2)·1. This difference is integral for every j≥k≥2, and its finite-coefficient and K/O actions are obtained from the integral derived correspondence, without lifting torsion sections. Here C_r is Pilloni’s operator T in §7; it is distinct from CG20 T and from either source’s individual numbered generators.
- Integral T and Q₂ on global forms: For j≥k≥2, T and Q₂ act O-linearly on M_(j,k)(O/ϖ^m), S_(j,k)(O/ϖ^m), and their K/O versions. T is the restriction of the integral minuscule correspondence, extended by Hartogs. Q₂ is the integral paramodular composite C_k minus (1+p²)p^(j−2). Its rational comparison and all-component expansion identify it with S5. The actions commute with coefficient transitions, tame deck transformations, prime-to-p Hecke operators and common fan refinements. Rationally they have the prescribed spherical normalization. No action of bare T₂ on these torsion spaces is inferred.
- Hasse equivariance at p: In characteristic p, multiplication by h commutes with T and Q₂ for weights j≥k≥3. The source and target symmetric degrees agree, and h has expansion 1. T reduces to U in both weights; Q₂ reduces to Z₂ in both, including weight (3,3). For k=2, T initially reduces to U+Z and Q₂ has the additional X₂ term at (2,2), so no such unrestricted commutation claim is made.

stages.title: Theta operators and low-weight injectivity
stages.description:
State theta only in characteristic p, with the GL₂ determinant twist in the contraction and no extra determinant in the vector Fourier coefficient. Prove the superspecial and negative-weight inputs separately, then give corrected scalar and vector injectivity ranges. Targets using the global secondary square root retain G2.

Targets:
- Integral symmetric-power contraction: Let d≥2 and let R be an algebra in which 2d(d+1) is invertible, in particular a characteristic-p algebra with p>d+2. For a free rank-two module E define con_d:Sym^d E⊗Sym²E→Sym^(d−2)E⊗(det E)² by the normalized second transvectant. In a frame x,y, con_d(f⊗g)=(f_xx g_yy−2f_xy g_xy+f_yy g_xx)/(2d(d+1)), with the indicated determinant-square tensor. This frame formula glues by GL₂-equivariance; changing to another source convention rescales by its explicitly identified unit. Under the chosen highest-weight inclusion, the vector x^d⊗y²−2x^(d−1)y⊗xy+x^(d−2)y²⊗x² maps to x^(d−2)⊗(x∧y)².
- Scalar and vector theta operators: Over k₀ of characteristic p>3 there is a scalar map Θ:M_(k,k)(k₀)→M_(k+p+1,k+p+1)(k₀), k≥2, whose Fourier coefficient is det(Q)a(F,Q). For d=j−k≥2 with p>d+2 and k≥2 there is a map θ₁:M_(j,k)(k₀)→M_(j+p−1,k+p+1)(k₀), whose coefficient is con_d(a(F,Q)⊗Q). Normalize the source differential operators by the unit making these exact formulas hold. The vector formula has no extra det(Q). Both preserve cusp forms. They are defined by the Gauss–Manin/Kodaira–Spencer construction with Hasse multiplication removing poles, and descend from principal neat tame level by étale descent. These are characteristic-p operators, with scalar extension to characteristic-p coefficient algebras; no construction modulo p² is asserted.
- Theta nonvanishing at superspecial points: If a scalar form of weight k≥2 is nonzero on SS and p does not divide k(2k−1), then ΘF≠0. For vector weight (j,k) with d=j−k≥2, p>d+2, a nonzero superspecial value gives θ₁F≠0 when j−3k is nonzero modulo p. In weight (6,2), the same conclusion holds for p>7 by choosing a local SL₂(F_p) frame in which the coefficient F₂ is nonzero; the local linear term has nonzero coefficient j−3=3. This is a change of fiber frame at the fixed point, not a Γ̄-action on global modular forms.
- Negative-weight section vanishing: At spherical good level over an algebraic closure, if a≥b and pa−b<0, then H⁰(Z_red,ω(a,b))=H⁰(S,ω(a,b))=H⁰(X₁,ω(a,b))=0; the same holds for their cusp subsheaves. On each P¹ component of Z_red, every summand of ω(a,b) has degree at most pa−b. A section zero on Z_red is divisible on S by its Cartier equation b₀ of weight m₀=(p²−1)/2; iterating decreases pa−b by (p−1)m₀ and Krull intersection forces zero. On X₁ repeat with the primary equation h, decreasing pa−b by (p−1)². The relevant divisors meet every component, and reducedness/density then propagates vanishing.
- Scalar theta injectivity in low weight: Let p>3, 2≤k≤p+1, k≠p−1 and p∤k(2k−1). Then Θ:M_(k,k)(k₀)→M_(k+p+1,k+p+1)(k₀) is injective, and so is its restriction to cusp forms. The exclusion k=p−1 is essential because h is nonzero with Θh=0. The result is over characteristic p, not an asserted injection modulo arbitrary powers of ϖ.
- Vector theta injectivity in weight (j,2): Let p>3 and 4≤j<p−1. Then θ₁:M_(j,2)(k₀)→M_(j+p−1,p+3)(k₀) is injective, also on cusp forms. This includes j=6 whenever the range permits it. The proof uses the closed nonordinary divisor S, not just its rank-one open, and does not infer that θ₁ annihilates every coefficient of singular Q.
- Small symmetric powers of SL₂(F_p): For 0≤d≤p−1 and an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, the natural representation Sym^d(k²) of SL₂(F_p) is irreducible. In the range d<p−1 needed here, every nonzero homogeneous polynomial P has a nonzero value at a primitive vector of F_p²; hence an SL₂(F_p) change of local frame can make its chosen extreme coefficient nonzero. The change is in a geometric fiber and is not a global action on the modular-form space.

stages.title: Ordinary p-adic forms and coefficient comparison
stages.description:
Use the full ordinary GL₂ Igusa tower requested from its existing owner. Fix action, Borel, character and limit order together, compare classical algebraic coefficients with continuous frame functions, and isolate the additional Klingen geometric normalization comparison from analytic control.

Targets:
- Degree-zero p-adic Siegel forms: Use the imported full ordinary genus-two Igusa tower Ig_(m,n) over X_m^ord. Put V_m=colim_n H⁰(Ig_(m,n),O) and V=lim_m V_m, with its p-adic topology and left function action (g·f)(ψ)=f(ψ∘g). Let U⁺ be the upper triangular unipotent subgroup of GL₂(Z_p). For a continuous character κ:Z_p×→O× and integer r, put χ_(κ,r)(diag(t₁,t₂))=κ(t₁)(t₁t₂)^r, and define V_(κ,r)={f∈V^(U⁺):t·f=χ_(κ,r)(t)f for every diagonal t}. Cusp forms use the inverse-image boundary ideal before taking colimits and inverse limits. Thus the algebraic specialization κ(t)=t^d has classical weight (d+r,r). This is Pilloni’s upper-unipotent convention: his weights are indexed from the bottom diagonal entry, κ′=(−k,−j), and −κ′ in those coordinates is exactly t₁^j t₂^k. The inverse-transpose frame map accounts for this character. An opposite-Borel convention must also reverse the two diagonal exponents.
- p-adic q-expansion and saturation: The canonical multiplicative trivialization of the split Mumford torus lifts each marked cusp to the full Igusa tower. For f∈V evaluate every g-translate at this lift, obtaining coefficients a_c(f,Q)(g) continuous in g∈GL₂(Z_p), locally constant at each finite coefficient level. For U⁺-invariant f these functions factor through GL₂(Z_p)/U⁺ with the stated left/right action convention. The family over every component and all frame translates is injective and saturated: f∈V[1/p] is integral iff all these coefficients are integral. The analogous finite-level statement has injective coefficient map with flat cokernel after the tower’s component-detection hypothesis, supplied by T5, is verified.
- Classical-to-p-adic comparison: Restriction to the ordinary formal locus followed by evaluation on its Igusa-induced differential frames defines an injective map M_(d+r,r)(O)→V_(t↦t^d,r), and similarly for cusp forms. It is compatible with classical and continuous-function-valued Fourier expansions under the algebraic symmetric-power coefficient inclusion. At finite coefficient level the analogous evaluation map is defined, but its injectivity is a separate property and is not inferred from the integral limit: integer-valued polynomial functions can vanish on all finite-level frames in characteristic p. The inverse limit map is injective by the expansion principle and the density of p-adic frames in the algebraic representation.
- Klingen ordinary coefficient operator: On the ordinary genus-two Igusa function space, normalize the Klingen degree-zero operator U_(p,2)^ord so that its formal coefficient action is Z₂=UZ: a(U_(p,2)^ord f,Q)=Σ_Mρ_d(M)a(f,M⁻¹·pQ) at an algebraic weight of symmetric degree d, and the corresponding finite-coset action on continuous frame functions at continuous weight. It preserves integral expansions and hence the integral function lattice by saturation. This operator is distinct from the diagonal formal U₂=−1+pX₂. The analytic Klingen operator p^(3−r)U_(Kli(p),1) and its identification under the overconvergent-to-Igusa embedding are supplied by HigherHidaAndColemanTheory; its raw normalization must be compared before using the same symbol.
